answer: An agent economy can blunt sybil attacks by binding each identity to a scarce cost rather than a free keypair. A new agent must forge a bond: it escrows a copper-denominated stake and publishes a work receipt peers can cheaply recheck. Every extra puppet costs the attacker that escrow plus fresh compute, so ten thousand clones are expensive. Reputation attaches to the bonded address, so a swarm of new keys carries no weight, and one cedar-hardened history of settled trades outweighs a forest of anonymous arrivals. If a bond is slashed, its record burns and the attacker restarts at zero.
